remaining_limitations: Raw TORGO and UASpeech audio corpora remain external dependencies; saved inventories preserve absolute source paths.
Original source signatures use path, file size and modification time rather than waveform-content hashes.
Notebook source is captured as present at freeze time; the historical run did not record a full notebook-file SHA256.
A byte-identical snapshot and cached representations preserve the completed result; bitwise retraining depends on the original runtime and hardware, which were not fully locked.
Read-only permissions and SHA256 detect accidental modification; a privileged user can change permissions.
Official UASpeech was studied in earlier versions; use locked zero-shot cross-corpus evaluation wording, not historically untouched prospective validation.
Requested dysarthria_v8(1).ipynb was not present; snapshotted the available current V8 notebook: dysarthria_v8.ipynb.

All three ablation-minus-reference balanced-accuracy speaker-bootstrap intervals include zero. The observed five-seed results do not establish a clear advantage for the reference pooling and layer mix; they also do not prove equivalence.
TORGO balanced accuracy is lower with five utterances (0.757) than with all available utterances (0.854); brief-speech deployment performance is weaker in this sample.
Verified matched-content analysis includes 25 of 28 M3 physical speakers because official transcript metadata did not support the others; it is a descriptive subset.
Diagnostic M2–M8 mean ROC-AUC spans 0.854–0.974; M3 remains the prespecified primary channel regardless of channel ranking.

UASpeech M3 threshold-free discrimination is strong (mean ROC-AUC 0.966), while the locked operating point is conservative (sensitivity 0.720, specificity 1.000); no UASpeech threshold adjustment was made.
